newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest electricity rises in continued cold.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest electricity rises in continued cold.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. rose Tuesday with continued cold temperatures through much of the region, brokers and marketers said.

Forecasts called for highs of between 10 and 24 degrees Fahrenheit on Wednesday for much of Minnesota, Wisconsin and Illinois, while longer-term outlooks called for near-normal temperatures through much of the Midwest from Feb 2 to 6 with some below normal temperatures in eastern areas.
Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Wednesday peak, non-firm power prices were pegged at $30.00-33.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) late Tuesday from $24.00-25.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Next-day peak MAPP power was said to have been trading near $25.00-26.00 earlier Tuesday but rose through the morning and early afternoon.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday were talked at $28.00-30.00 from $22.00-25.00 on Monday for Tuesday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
MAIN off peak Wednesday power was said to be unchanged at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday were reported to be discussed at $26.00-30.00 through much of the region from 20.50-21.50 in the south and near $25.00 in the north on Monday, the sources said.

In ECAR, Consumers Power Co continued to investigate the cause of a shutdown at its 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan and had not set a date for the plant to resume electricity production.
The plant was shut Jan 23 after a problem with electrical equipment at a main generator.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was assessed at $22.80-23.00 from $22.60-22.80 on Monday.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were pegged at $34.00-35.00 from $30.50-32.00 in the north and at $27.00-29.00 from $25.00-26.00 in the south, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were loosely assessed higher at $17.00-19.00 in the north and steady at $13.00-15.00 in the south, the sources said.
February SPP was assessed at $23.25-23.90 from $23.00-23.50 on Monday, while March was pegged near $21.00 and July/August at $27.00-27.25 per MWh, the sources said.
